instruction.text: We are now in the 1900s. Which two pieces of technology helped make sport more popular?
These two men in the 1920s are having a conversation. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Hi David! Would you like to come and watch a ((++tennis music)) match with me?
Unfortunately, I ((can ++can’t)) make it this time James.
But, I have heard that the match will be broadcast on the ((++radio patio)), so I can listen to it at home.
On the radio? Wow, that’s new! So many more ((++people animals)) will now be able to follow along and stay updated with the result.
Exactly! Although I can’t be there in person, I can still ((++listen watch)) along and follow the match.

feedback.finish: From 1927, the BBC began broadcasting live sport on public radios. For the first time, people could follow events without having to be there in person.

atoms.b: In ((++1937 2017)), the first sporting event was broadcast on television by the BBC. Early televisions were big, ((cheap ++expensive)) and bad quality.
By the 1950s, televisions became cheaper, and ((less ++more)) events were broadcast, bringing fans together and turning many athletes into ((++celebrities clowns)).
In the 1960s, sport was shown in ((++colour black_and_white)) for the first time. This made it more ((++exciting boring)) and encouraged more people to watch.
By the 1990s, most ((gardens ++homes)) in the UK had a television. Sports were watched by millions of people and had become an important part of national culture.

instruction.text: Select the image of a modern stadium.

feedback.finish: With more people now following sports, teams were making more money. This money paid for bigger and better stadiums around the UK, and more fans could go and watch their favourite teams play.

instruction.text: Drag the sponsor onto the football shirt.

feedback.finish: Companies also began sponsoring sports teams, meaning they gave them money to put their logos on the players’ shirts.

atoms.b: Increased interest in ((animal ++professional)) sports also encouraged more normal people to begin playing in their free time.
Throughout the UK, local clubs and ((++sports_centres supermarkets)) were built for people to play many different sports.
Playing sport became more popular for people of all ages and ((beaches ++backgrounds)) as a way to socialise and stay healthy.
